mzLibR

mzLib for R — mass spectrometry and proteomics, with no .NET to install and no package dependencies.

The third sibling of pyMzLib and mzLibRust, over the same language-neutral bridge, so all three agree field for field.

# Read a mass-spectrometry data file: mzML, Thermo .raw, Bruker .d, timsTOF .d, MGF, msalign
scans <- readers_read_spectra("run.mzML", ms_order = 2, limit = 5)
scans$scan_count                                    # total in the file, before the MS-level filter
scans$records[, c("one_based_scan_number", "retention_time", "selected_ion_mz")]

files <- pride_list_files("PXD000001")
files[files$size_mb < 5 & files$downloadable, c("file_name", "size_mb", "category")]

digest <- peptidoform_fragments("P02768")           # serum albumin, at mzLib's defaults
digest_fragments_by_series(digest)

quant <- flashlfq_quantify("AllPSMs.psmtsv", c("run_3.mzML", "run_4.mzML"),
                           match_between_runs = TRUE)
transfers <- flashlfq_mbr_peaks(quant)              # read peaks, never the peptide roll-up

What it does

pride_* List and download from the PRIDE Archive, with mzLib’s paging and URL resolution, and check a download against the MD5 and exact size PRIDE recorded with pride_file_checksums()
peptidoform_* Fetch a UniProt entry, apply its modifications, digest, and fragment; convert MetaMorpheus full sequences to Unimod or ProForma with peptidoform_convert()
flashlfq_* Label-free quantification with match-between-runs
readers_* Read spectra from mzML, Thermo .raw, Bruker .d, timsTOF .d, MGF and msalign with readers_read_spectra(); identify and read every file type mzLib knows, search results included — readers_read_records() reads any of them into that format’s own fields, while readers_read_results(), readers_read_features(), readers_read_matches() and readers_read_spectra() project the four cross-format views
library_* Read mzLib’s .msl spectral libraries with library_read() and library_read_many(): every precursor with its retention time in iRT or minutes per row, and its fragment ions on request; calibrate a run’s minutes onto a library’s iRT scale, and back, with library_calibrate_rt()
proteins_* What an accession is (organism, taxon, GO terms, Ensembl ids) with proteins_read(), which gene it resolves to against a pinned Ensembl release with proteins_resolve_genes(), whether a peptide is unique to one protein or gene with proteins_classify_peptides(), and the Gene Ontology terms of every MetaMorpheus protein group, every member kept, against a pinned GO release with proteins_annotate_go(); carry a residue position to an isoform or ortholog with proteins_align(), read an accession into entry, isoform and variants with proteins_parse_accessions(), build an Ensembl Compara orthology snapshot with proteins_build_orthology(), and carry a residue across species through Compara’s gene-tree alignment with proteins_map_residues()
sdrf_* Read SDRF-Proteomics experimental-design files with sdrf_read(), and pool several into one table with provenance with sdrf_pool(); check them with sdrf_validate(), sdrf_assess() and sdrf_lint(), get each sample’s ages in years with sdrf_samples(), and read the label-free design a quantification takes, or every reason there is none, with sdrf_design(), and its isobaric counterpart with sdrf_isobaric_design(); cut an SDRF to the files one search read with sdrf_restrict(). Use these rather than readers_read_records(), which joins each SDRF row into one string that cannot be split back apart
isobaric_* TMT, TMTpro, iTRAQ and DiLeu kits with every channel’s label and theoretical reporter-ion m/z, from mzLib’s own table, with isobaric_kits()
stats_* limma’s moderated t-test (lmFit + eBayes(legacy = TRUE)) with stats_fit(), which also tests contrasts with confidence intervals and offers mzLib’s marginal-likelihood prior; Benjamini-Hochberg with stats_adjust(); DerSimonian-Laird random-effects meta-analysis with stats_meta(); Fisher and Stouffer p-value combination with stats_combine_p(); Spearman correlation with a trait, plain or partial, with stats_correlate(); a logistic model per feature of a detection table with stats_fit_logistic(); a mixed model per feature with a random intercept per group with stats_fit_mixed(), and on a latent scale from measured and counted samples with stats_fit_latent_mixed(), through a detection link stats_fit_link() fits; and entrapment FDP estimates with stats_entrapment_fdp() - computed by mzLib and held to limma, metafor, glm(), nlme, lme4’s glmer(), glmmTMB and cor.test()
diff_* A sample sheet to mzLib’s design matrix per stratum, equal to R’s model.matrix(), with every default contrast and whether these samples can estimate it, and the design and contrasts files stats_fit() reads, with diff_design(); a FlashLFQ or MetaMorpheus peptide table to every peptide in every sample, log2 intensity or NA with the reason, with mzLib’s shared-peptide normalization, with diff_observations()
ptmqtl_* PTM site occupancy in every run with each cell’s state (a censored cell is never a 0) with ptmqtl_occupancy(), modification pairs on one molecule or co-varying across runs with ptmqtl_pairs() (one-form runs as tied bounds, and given each run’s depth, on request), and a per-run trait’s effect on the log odds of occupancy (natural or log2) with a random intercept per replicate with ptmqtl_trait_effects()

Installing 

install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("smith-chem-wisc/mzLibR")
mzlibr_install_bridge()          # ~140 MB, asks first, verifies a SHA-256

The bridge is a self-contained executable carrying its own .NET runtime, so no .NET installation is required. It cannot ship inside the package — CRAN’s limit is about 5 MB — so mzlibr_install_bridge() fetches it on your say-so and caches it. If you already have one, point at it instead and skip the download:

Sys.setenv(MZLIB_BRIDGE = "/path/to/mzlib-bridge")

That override is also how you relink a modified mzLib without rebuilding this package, which LGPL section 4 requires mzLibR to permit.

No dependencies, and why that made it better

mzLibR imports nothing but base R. (limma and metafor are suggested, for the tests alone: when they are installed, the tests hold stats_fit() and stats_meta() to them.) jsonlite and processx would have been the obvious floor, and dropping them was a correctness decision more than a portability one:

  • jsonlite auto-simplifies, and JSON null becomes R NULL. A NULL assigned into a list deletes the element, so a protein-intensity vector would not come back wrong, it would come back short, silently — and FlashLFQ emits null for precisely the protein it could not resolve. mzLibR’s own reader never simplifies and reads null as NA, which occupies its slot like any other value.
  • processx was for the subprocess timeout. system2() has had one since R 3.5.0, and delivers stdin at the same time, which was verified against the real bridge before the dependency was dropped.

Requires R >= 3.5.0, set solely by system2(timeout=).

Things that will otherwise catch you

Every one of these is documented on the argument that causes it, and pinned by a test.

  • A compressed file’s extension is .gz, not what it is compressed from. PXD000001’s peak list is …pride.mgf.gz, so filtering on ".mgf" matches nothing.
  • PRIDE’s API manifest is incomplete. On 2026-10-21 it listed 9 of PXD000001’s 14 files, omitting the two largest; pride_list_ftp_files() lists them all. And file_size_bytes is the decompressed size for some compressed files — 2.75x off for that MGF.
  • A PRIDE download is not checked against PRIDE’s record. Compare a file that matters with pride_file_checksums(): its size_bytes is the exact download length and its md5 the digest, which the manifest’s checksum (a SHA-1, when present) is not.
  • mzLib’s "trypsin|P" applies the Keil rule and plain "trypsin", its default, does not — the reverse of the MaxQuant and Mascot convention. 195 peptides against 202 on albumin.
  • mzLib’s default min_length silently discards everything shorter — albumin goes from 202 distinct sequences to 257 at min_length = 1.
  • peptidoform_fragments() leaves its defaults to mzLib. An argument you leave NULL is not sent, and mzLib’s own default applies; with no dissociation, the bridge uses HCD until mzLib names one (mzLib#1488). The result says which protease and dissociation type were used.
  • Read peaks, never the peptide roll-up, for match-between-runs. The roll-up drops most transfers — 140 true against 52 shown — and a whole run’s can vanish.
  • A peptide intensity of 0 and a protein intensity of NA mean different things. 0 is “not measured in this run”; NA is “FlashLFQ could not resolve a number”. NA is the rare outcome (2 proteins) and 0 the common one (847).
  • max_threads defaults to 1 here, where pyMzLib and mzLibRust use -1 (every core). The multithreaded nondeterminism that set this default (mzLib#1111) was fixed by mzLib#1155, which the pinned bridge includes; the default stays until -1 is re-measured. See ?flashlfq_quantify.
  • readers_identify() does not validate contents, and a TRUE from is_quantifiable is not permission — it reports what mzLib’s interface offers, not that the numbers are comparable.

Documentation

Every help page for a function that calls the bridge carries that call’s facts - every parameter and returned column with its unit and what NA means, the errors it raises, the same call in pyMzLib and mzLibRust - generated from the bridge’s per-verb specs, and every page has an example that R CMD check runs. ?mzlib_error explains the condition classes.

  • The documentation site - the help pages and an article per module: reading files, spectral libraries, SDRF, isobaric kits, PRIDE, protein databases and GO, peptidoforms, FlashLFQ, differential abundance, differential design and observations, and PTM occupancy. The articles are also the package’s vignettes, browseVignettes("mzLibR"), and R CMD check runs every one.
  • docs/reference-facts.md - for contributors: how the help pages are generated from the specs and checked against them.
  • docs/name-parity.md — every function, parameter and column checked mechanically against pyMzLib and against the wire. Generated, not written.
  • docs/test-parity.md — what the suite covers against the parent’s, what R’s semantics made unnecessary, and what is deliberately not run.

?pride_list_files, ?peptidoform_fragments, ?flashlfq_quantify and ?readers_identify carry the detail.

Upstream issues found by this port

An mzLib bug becomes an mzLib issue; a workaround in a binding leaves every other consumer broken. See mzLib #1106, #1109, #1110, #1111, #1112, #1113.
